ordered_diagnoses: Signet-ring cell carcinoma of the bladder

s1.syndrome_frame: intermittent painless hematuria with clot passage in an elderly patient with underlying medical conditions
salient_findings: painless hematuria with passage of clots
polypoidal mass arising from the bladder dome
exophytic solid tumor on the anterior fundal wall of the bladder
adenocarcinoma with mucinous and signet-ring cell components on histopathology
key_facts: denies dysuria, frequency, or other lower urinary tract symptoms
serum creatinine and other biochemical parameters within normal limits
transabdominal ultrasonography showed a 2.9 × 2.5 × 2.4 cm polypoidal mass
cystoscopy demonstrated an exophytic solid tumor

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a polypoidal mass in the bladder and histopathological analysis revealing adenocarcinoma composed of mucinous and signet-ring cell components is consistent with primary adenocarcinoma of the bladder, a rare variant of bladder cancer.
